q: Which French town hosted the first Winter Olympics in 1924?
x: The event was originally called 'International Winter Sports Week' and was only declared the first Winter Olympics afterward.

q: How far is the penalty spot from the goal line in soccer?
x: That is about 11 meters. The distance was set in the early rules adopted in 1902, when the penalty kick was introduced.

q: Which country won the 1994 FIFA World Cup, beating Italy on penalties?
x: It was the first World Cup final decided by a penalty shootout. Italy's Roberto Baggio missed the decisive kick.

q: Which team did France beat 3-0 in the 1998 World Cup final?
x: The match was played at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis. Brazil's Ronaldo had suffered a mysterious fit hours before kickoff.

q: Which Swedish tennis player won five consecutive Wimbledon titles from 1976 to 1980?
x: Borg retired at just 26 years old. His 1980 final against John McEnroe included a famous 18-16 tiebreak.

q: Which golf major is traditionally awarded with the Claret Jug?
x: The Open is the oldest golf major, first played in 1860. It is always held on a links course in Britain.

q: What is the diameter of a standard basketball hoop's rim?
x: The hoop is 18 inches (45.7 cm) across, while a regulation basketball is only about 9.5 inches wide.

q: What is the trophy of the Rugby World Cup called?
x: The trophy is named after William Webb Ellis, who according to legend invented rugby by picking up the ball and running with it.

q: What is a batter's score of 100 runs called in cricket?
x: Scoring a century is a major milestone. A score of 200 is a double century, and the batter's team is often applauded loudly.

q: Which country won the first Rugby World Cup, in 1987?
x: New Zealand beat France 29-9 in the final at Eden Park in Auckland. The tournament was co-hosted with Australia.

q: Which British runner was the first to break the four-minute mile, in 1954?
x: Bannister ran 3:59.4 at Iffley Road in Oxford. He was a medical student at the time and later became a neurologist.

q: Which American swimmer won seven gold medals at the 1972 Olympics?
x: Spitz set a world record in each of his seven events. His total stood as the most golds at one Games until 2008.

q: Which German tennis player won the 1988 calendar-year Grand Slam and an Olympic gold?
x: Graf's 1988 'Golden Slam' of all four majors plus Olympic gold in Seoul remains one of tennis's greatest feats.

q: Which Australian tennis legend won the calendar-year Grand Slam in both 1962 and 1969?
x: Laver is the only man to complete the calendar-year Grand Slam twice, with the second coming after tennis opened to professionals.

q: How long is the pitch between the wickets in cricket?
x: This distance is one chain, a unit of land measurement used since 1700, and equals about 20 meters.

q: How many players per team are on the field in Australian rules football?
x: Each team also has four substitutes on the interchange bench. The oval field can be up to 185 meters long.

q: Which basketball team did Bill Russell win 11 NBA championships with?
x: Russell won the titles in 13 seasons from 1957 to 1969, and for the last two he also served as the team's player-coach.

q: Which New York Yankees first baseman was nicknamed 'the Iron Horse'?
x: Gehrig played 2,130 consecutive games between 1925 and 1939. He ended the streak when illness began to weaken him.

q: In 1947, Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball's color barrier with which team?
x: His number 42 was retired across all Major League teams in 1997. The Dodgers later moved to Los Angeles.

q: Ayrton Senna, a three-time Formula One champion, was from which country?
x: Senna won his titles in 1988, 1990 and 1991 and was known for his skill in wet conditions.

q: Which German driver won five consecutive Formula One titles from 2000 to 2004?
x: Schumacher won those titles driving for Ferrari, ending a long title drought for the Italian team that had lasted since 1979.

q: The Daytona 500 stock car race is held in which US state?
x: Held at Daytona International Speedway each February, the race is the opening event of the NASCAR season.

q: Which Italian car maker uses a prancing horse as its racing emblem?
x: Enzo Ferrari adopted the horse after meeting the parents of an Italian air ace, Francesco Baracca, who had painted it on his plane.

q: The 24 Hours of Le Mans endurance race takes place in which country?
x: The race was first held in 1923 on public roads near the town of Le Mans. Teams of drivers share one car for a full day.

q: In golf, what is the name for a score of three strokes under par on one hole?
x: The term is the Americanized form of 'double eagle'. It is extremely rare, as it usually requires holing out on a par 5.

q: Which golfer was nicknamed 'the Golden Bear'?
x: Nicklaus won 18 major championships in a career spanning more than two decades. He won his last Masters at age 46.

q: Which Australian golfer was nicknamed 'the Great White Shark'?
x: Norman won the Open Championship twice and held the world number one ranking for 331 weeks.

q: Which team won the first Cricket World Cup in 1975?
x: The West Indies beat Australia in the final at Lord's, with captain Clive Lloyd scoring a century. They also won in 1979.

q: Which country won the 1983 Cricket World Cup, beating the West Indies in the final?
x: India defended a low total of 183 at Lord's, a huge upset. The win helped spark cricket's popularity across India.

q: Which Australian batsman finished his Test career with an average of 99.94?
x: Bradman needed just four runs in his final innings to average 100 but was bowled for a duck.

q: Which city hosted the 1900 Olympics, the first Games in which women competed?
x: The 1900 Games were spread over five months as part of the World's Fair. Tennis player Charlotte Cooper became the first female Olympic champion.

q: Who founded the International Olympic Committee in 1894 and revived the modern Games?
x: The French educator was inspired by England's Wenlock Olympian Games. His heart is buried at Olympia in Greece.

q: How many players per team are in the water in a water polo match, including the goalkeeper?
x: Water polo players must tread water throughout the match and may only hold the ball with one hand, except the goalkeeper.

q: How many points is a drop goal worth in rugby union?
x: England's Jonny Wilkinson scored a famous drop goal to win the 2003 World Cup final.

q: What is the name of the traditional Maori war dance performed by the New Zealand national rugby team?
x: The All Blacks' best-known haka is 'Ka Mate', which they have performed before test matches for over a century.

q: In which athletics event did Dick Fosbury revolutionize technique at the 1968 Olympics?
x: He went over the bar backwards and headfirst, a style now known worldwide as the Fosbury Flop. It replaced older straddle styles.

q: Which American won the first women's Olympic marathon, at the 1984 Los Angeles Games?
x: Benoit entered the stadium to a roar from the crowd and won by over 400 meters. The women's marathon was first added in 1984.

q: Which Ethiopian ran barefoot to win the marathon at the 1960 Rome Olympics?
x: Bikila won gold in Rome in bare feet and won again in Tokyo in 1964, this time wearing shoes. He set a world best in both races.

q: Which Czechoslovak runner won the 5,000 m, 10,000 m and marathon at the 1952 Olympics?
x: Zatopek entered his first marathon in Helsinki and won, after a few words of advice from British rival Jim Peters.

q: Which Finnish distance runner, nicknamed the 'Flying Finn', won nine Olympic gold medals?
x: Nurmi won his golds between 1920 and 1928. He was known for carrying a stopwatch to pace himself in races.

q: Which fruit is traditionally served with cream at the Wimbledon Championships?
x: Fans consume more than 30 tonnes of strawberries during the two-week tournament.

q: What is the maximum number of sets in a men's Grand Slam singles match?
x: The women's matches use a best-of-three format. A man must win three sets to win a match.

q: Which Parisian stadium hosts the French Open?
x: The stadium was named after Roland Garros, a French aviator and World War I pilot. It was built in 1928 for a Davis Cup match.

q: Which 17-year-old German won Wimbledon in 1985?
x: Becker became the youngest men's singles champion at Wimbledon, and also the first unseeded winner.

q: Which national team, led by Johan Cruyff, popularized 'Total Football' in the 1970s?
x: In Total Football any outfield player can take over the role of a teammate. The Dutch reached the 1974 and 1978 World Cup finals.

q: Which English captain lifted the World Cup trophy in 1966?
x: Moore received the trophy from the Queen at Wembley. He wiped his muddy hands on his shorts before shaking her hand.

q: Who scored a hat-trick for England in the 1966 World Cup final?
x: Hurst's second goal, which bounced off the crossbar, is still debated. His hat-trick sealed a 4-2 win after extra time.

q: Which Spanish club plays its home matches at Camp Nou?
x: Camp Nou opened in 1957 and means 'new field' in Catalan. It is among the largest club stadiums in Europe.

q: Which English club plays its home matches at Old Trafford?
x: Old Trafford is nicknamed 'the Theatre of Dreams'. It is in Greater Manchester, near the city center.

q: Biathlon combines cross-country skiing with which other discipline?
x: Missed targets add penalty loops or time. The sport grew out of military patrol training in Scandinavia.

q: What type of rock are curling stones traditionally made from?
x: The finest curling stones come from a single quarry on Ailsa Craig, a Scottish island. Each stone weighs about 20 kg.

q: How many players make up a curling team?
x: The positions are called the lead, second, third (or vice-skip) and skip. The skip calls the strategy.

q: How long is a minor penalty in ice hockey?
x: The offending player sits in the penalty box while the team plays shorthanded. A major penalty lasts five minutes.

q: How many major championships are there in men's professional golf?
x: The four majors are the Masters, the US Open, the Open Championship and the PGA Championship.

q: What is the maximum number of clubs a golfer may carry during a round?
x: The limit was adopted in 1938. Before that, some golfers carried as many as 25 clubs.

q: Which trophy is awarded to the winner of the Super Bowl?
x: The silver football-shaped trophy was renamed in honor of Green Bay Packers coach Vince Lombardi after his death in 1970.

q: How many innings are in a standard Major League Baseball game?
x: Tied games go to extra innings until one team leads at the end of a full inning.

q: What is it called when a baseball batter receives four balls and advances to first base?
x: The official term is 'base on balls'. A pitcher who walks many batters is said to have poor control.

q: In which US city is Fenway Park, one of baseball's oldest stadiums?
x: Fenway Park opened in 1912 and is the home of the Red Sox. Its tall left-field wall is known as the Green Monster.

q: In which US city is Wrigley Field, home of the Cubs?
x: Wrigley Field opened in 1914 and is famous for its ivy-covered outfield walls. It did not have lights for night games until 1988.

q: How many seconds is the shot clock in NBA basketball?
x: The 24-second clock was introduced in 1954 to speed up the game, which had become slow and low scoring.

q: What is the name of Major League Baseball's annual championship series?
x: Despite the name, only teams from the United States and Canada take part. The first modern series was in 1903. It is also nicknamed the Fall Classic.

q: Which of cycling's Grand Tours takes place in Italy?
x: The Giro leader wears a pink jersey, because the sponsoring newspaper, La Gazzetta dello Sport, is printed on pink paper.

q: What does the polka-dot jersey signify in the Tour de France?
x: The jersey is white with red dots. It is awarded to the rider who earns the most points on the major mountain climbs.

q: On which river does the annual Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race take place?
x: The race has been held since 1829 on a 4.2-mile stretch in London between Putney and Mortlake.

q: Which fencing weapon, along with foil and sabre, is used in Olympic competition?
x: Fencing has been in every modern Olympics. In epee, a touch can be scored anywhere on the body.

q: What is the highest rank in professional sumo wrestling?
x: A yokozuna cannot be demoted and is expected to retire if they can no longer perform. They wear a special white rope belt.

q: In which African country did Muhammad Ali fight George Foreman in the 1974 'Rumble in the Jungle'?
x: The fight took place in Kinshasa, now in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ali used his 'rope-a-dope' tactic to win by knockout.

q: Which American heavyweight boxer was nicknamed the 'Brown Bomber'?
x: Louis held the heavyweight title for nearly 12 years, from 1937 to 1949, defending it a record 25 times.

q: Which Soviet gymnast charmed audiences at the 1972 Olympics and popularized a backward somersault on the beam?
x: Korbut won three gold medals in 1972. Her fame helped spark a boom in gymnastics around the world.

q: How many events make up the women's heptathlon?
x: The events are spread over two days. The men's equivalent, the decathlon, has ten events.

q: Which Australian runner lit the Olympic cauldron at the 2000 Sydney Games?
x: Freeman went on to win the 400 m gold in front of a home crowd, after emerging from a pool of water in the ceremony.

q: Which North London club is nicknamed 'the Gunners'?
x: The club was founded in 1886 by workers at the Royal Arsenal armaments factory in Woolwich.

q: Pele spent most of his club career at which Brazilian club?
x: Pele joined Santos at age 15 and stayed for almost two decades. He also played in the United States for the New York Cosmos.

q: What was the original name of the UEFA Champions League when it began in 1955?
x: The tournament was proposed by the French sports newspaper L'Equipe. Real Madrid won the first five editions.

q: At which Olympics did the American 'Dream Team' of NBA stars first compete?
x: Before 1992, only amateurs were allowed to play for the US team. The Dream Team won gold by an average of more than 40 points.

q: In cricket, what does LBW stand for?
x: A batter can be out LBW if the ball would have hit the stumps but was blocked by the batter's leg or body.

q: How many legal deliveries are in a standard over in cricket?
x: In the past some countries used eight-ball overs, including Australia until the 1979-80 season.

q: Which country joined the Five Nations rugby tournament in 2000 to make it the Six Nations?
x: Italy beat Scotland 34-20 in its debut match. The tournament had previously included England, Scotland, Ireland, Wales and France.

q: Which fly-half kicked England's winning drop goal in the 2003 Rugby World Cup final?
x: The kick came in the final seconds of extra time against Australia in Sydney, giving England a 20-17 victory.

q: Which country won the 1995 Rugby World Cup on home soil?
x: South Africa beat New Zealand 15-12 in extra time. Nelson Mandela famously presented the trophy wearing a Springbok jersey.

q: What is the maximum break in a frame of snooker?
x: It requires potting all 15 reds with 15 blacks, then all six colors in order. It is known as a maximum break.

q: What is the highest score possible with three darts in one turn?
x: It is achieved with three treble 20s. Many pub players dream of hitting it, and crowds traditionally cheer a loud 'one hundred and eighty!'

q: In which sport did Eddie 'the Eagle' Edwards become a cult hero at the 1988 Winter Olympics?
x: Michael 'Eddie' Edwards from England was the only British ski jumper at the Calgary Games and finished last in both events.

q: Which music did British ice dancers Torvill and Dean skate to for their 1984 Olympic gold?
x: Their Sarajevo routine to Ravel's Bolero earned a perfect set of nine 6.0 marks for artistic impression.

q: Which team did the United States beat in the 1980 'Miracle on Ice' hockey game?
x: A team of American college players upset the favored Soviets 4-3 at Lake Placid. They then beat Finland to win gold.

q: Which basketball player scored 100 points in a single NBA game in 1962?
x: Chamberlain's Philadelphia Warriors beat the New York Knicks 169-147 in Hershey, Pennsylvania. The game was not televised.

q: Which NBA team plays its home games at Madison Square Garden?
x: The current Garden is the fourth building to use the name. It also hosts boxing, concerts and ice hockey.

q: Which jersey number did hockey star Wayne Gretzky wear, later retired across the NHL?
x: Gretzky's number 99 was retired by the whole league in 2000. He was nicknamed 'The Great One'.

q: The Cy Young Award honors excellence in which baseball role?
x: It is named after Cy Young, who won 511 games as a pitcher, a total that is unlikely ever to be beaten.

q: How many yards must an American football offense gain to earn a first down?
x: The offense has four chances, called downs, to advance 10 yards. If it fails, the ball goes to the other team.

q: How long is an American football field between the two goal lines?
x: The end zones add 10 yards at each end, so the whole field is 120 yards. The field is 53 and a third yards wide.

q: Which Olympic champion swimmer later starred as Tarzan in Hollywood films?
x: Weissmuller won five Olympic golds in the 1920s and later made 12 Tarzan films.

q: Which Asian city hosted the 1964 Summer Olympics, the first Games held in Asia?
x: The Tokyo Games were the first broadcast internationally by satellite. Judo made its Olympic debut there.

q: Which Norwegian town hosted the 1994 Winter Olympics?
x: The 1994 Games were held only two years after the 1992 edition, when the schedule was changed so Winter and Summer Games alternate every two years.

q: Which Italian club is nicknamed 'the Old Lady'?
x: Juventus is based in Turin and wears black and white stripes. It has won more Italian league titles than any other club.

q: Which Argentine won five Formula One world titles in the 1950s?
x: Fangio won his titles with four different teams. He was nicknamed 'El Chueco', Spanish for 'the bowlegged one'.

q: Which Parisian avenue is the traditional finish of the Tour de France?
x: The race has finished on the Champs-Elysees since 1975. Before that, it ended at the Parc des Princes or Vel d'Hiv.

q: Which Soviet goalkeeper, nicknamed the 'Black Spider', is a legend of European football?
x: Yashin wore all black and is said to have saved well over 100 penalties. He won the Ballon d'Or in 1963.

q: What does the winner of the Indianapolis 500 traditionally drink in victory lane?
x: The custom began in 1936, when Louis Meyer asked for buttermilk, which his mother had told him refreshes on hot days.
